intro: Dallas ran over Philadelphia on Monday night and the Eagles have now lost five straight. Cincinnati scored 35 unanswered against Baltimore, and Minnesota stays unbeaten as it heads to Detroit on Sunday. 160 stories across all 32 teams.

top.label: Biggest Story
top.headline: Cowboys run past Eagles 38-21, Philadelphia loses a fifth straight
top.dek: Dallas ran for 204 yards, scored on seven of nine drives and moved to 3-4 on Monday night. The Eagles fell to 2-5 and have allowed at least 375 yards in every game of the skid.

top.label: Injury Watch
top.headline: Bears lose Cole Kmet for the season with a knee injury
top.dek: Kmet went down late in the fourth quarter of Chicago's 30-24 win over New England and is on injured reserve. Colston Loveland and rookie Sam Roush take on bigger roles at tight end.

top.label: Player Spotlight
top.headline: Joe Burrow throws four second-half touchdowns in Baltimore
top.dek: Burrow finished 22 of 30 for 292 yards, and all four scores came after halftime. He went 16 of 18 for 249 yards in that half as Cincinnati erased a 13-0 deficit and won 35-13.

top.label: Stat of the Day
top.headline: 8: Justin Herbert's interceptions, the most in the NFL
top.dek: The 0-6 Chargers quarterback has five touchdowns, 10 turnovers and 21 sacks taken, second most in the league. Jim Harbaugh said Herbert has played with desperation at times.

top.label: What's Next
top.headline: Unbeaten Vikings visit the Lions on Sunday
top.dek: Minnesota, the league's only 6-0 team, plays at 4-2 Detroit on Nov. 1 at 1 p.m. ET on Fox. The Bills, Packers and 49ers follow, so the next four weeks show how real this start is.

teams.name: Buffalo Bills
teams.headline: Bills return from bye to face Ravens

stories.text: Bills come off the bye with the East lead and a Lamar Jackson question
stories.summary: Buffalo sits at 5-1 and hosts Baltimore on Sunday after a week off. The Ravens are 4-3 and Lamar Jackson, out three games with a high ankle sprain, is expected to try to return. His status likely stays unclear until Wednesday, so Buffalo has to prepare for him and for Tyler Huntley.

stories.text: Bills expect to be mostly healthy after the bye
stories.summary: Buffalo comes out of the bye expecting to be relatively healthy across the board. Receiver DJ Moore has been the main name on the injury list, with a shoulder issue that kept him to four of the first six games. Watch Wednesday's practice report to see where he stands.

stories.text: James Cook is carrying the Bills ground game
stories.summary: Cook has 627 rushing yards on 117 carries, third in the NFL through six games. Josh Allen is Buffalo's second-leading rusher with 240 yards on 48 carries. Coach Joe Brady has said he wants to keep Cook healthy for the full season.

stories.text: 17: Josh Allen's touchdowns, 10 more than Lamar Jackson's
stories.summary: Allen has 17 total touchdowns this season. Jackson has seven, according to StatMuse numbers cited before the Week 8 meeting. Allen also leads the NFL in total touchdowns.

stories.text: Bills host Ravens Sunday at 1 p.m. ET on CBS
stories.summary: Buffalo plays Baltimore at Highmark Stadium on Sunday, Nov. 1, at 1:00 p.m. ET on CBS. The Ravens blew a 13-0 halftime lead in a 35-13 loss to Cincinnati. Watch whether Jackson plays and whether Buffalo's pass defense holds up.

teams.name: Miami Dolphins
teams.headline: Dolphins finally win, beat Jets 28-25

stories.text: Dolphins get their first win, 28-25 over the Jets
stories.summary: Miami beat New York at MetLife Stadium for its first victory of 2026 and the first under coach Jeff Hafley. The Dolphins led 21-7 at halftime and sealed it with a fourth-and-1 tush push near the two-minute warning. It was also the first game all year in which Miami held a lead.

stories.text: Achane is gone for the year, Douglas is back
stories.summary: De'Von Achane tore his left ACL in September and went on injured reserve, leaving Ollie Gordon and Jaylen Wright as the only running backs. Receiver Caleb Douglas returned from a three-game absence with a leg injury and scored twice against the Jets.

stories.text: Ollie Gordon keeps producing in Achane's place
stories.summary: Gordon ran 25 times for 103 yards and a touchdown against the Jets. Over the last three games he has 291 rushing yards at 5.6 yards per carry with three rushing touchdowns. Miami has leaned on him since Achane went down.

stories.text: 23.4%: Chop Robinson leads the NFL in pressure rate
stories.summary: Robinson had five pressures on 23 pass rushes against the Jets, per Next Gen Stats. That puts his season pressure rate at 23.4 percent, tops in the league among players with at least 100 pass rushes. He also sacked Geno Smith for a 12-yard loss in the fourth quarter.

stories.text: Dolphins host Patriots Sunday at 4:25 p.m. ET on CBS
stories.summary: Miami hosts New England on Sunday, Nov. 1, at 4:25 p.m. ET on CBS, its second straight AFC East game. The Patriots are coming off a Thursday night loss in Chicago. Watch whether Malik Willis and the offense can repeat their 28-point day.

teams.name: New England Patriots
teams.headline: Patriots fall to Bears, 30-24

stories.text: Bears end the Patriots' three-game win streak, 30-24
stories.summary: New England lost on Thursday night in Chicago and dropped to 4-3. The Patriots committed 10 penalties and missed 16 tackles. Mike Vrabel said the tackling was not good enough against a team like Chicago.

stories.text: Patriots line is down to third-string guards
stories.summary: New England started third- or fourth-string guards in Chicago, with Mike Onwenu and Greg Van Roten on injured reserve. Tackle Morgan Moses played through a foot problem. The team has used 10 different offensive line combinations this season, versus seven in all of 2025.

stories.text: Drake Maye throws for 321 yards in the loss
stories.summary: Maye went 24 of 31 for 321 yards, two touchdowns and one interception, and he ran for a score. He later said he wished he could take back the second-quarter end zone pass that Chicago picked off. The Bears drove 80 yards for a touchdown after that turnover.

stories.text: 16: tackles the Patriots missed against Chicago
stories.summary: New England missed 16 tackles and gave up 149 yards after the catch. The defense also allowed 85 rushing yards after contact. Vrabel pointed to tackling as the main problem.

stories.text: Patriots visit Dolphins Sunday at 4:25 p.m. ET on CBS
stories.summary: New England plays at Miami on Sunday, Nov. 1, at 4:25 p.m. ET on CBS. The Dolphins just won their first game of the year. The Patriots need to fix their tackling and find answers for a banged-up offensive line.

teams.name: New York Jets
teams.headline: Jets lose to winless Dolphins, 28-25

stories.text: Jets fall to the Dolphins at home, 28-25
stories.summary: New York dropped to 2-5 with a home loss to a Miami team that had not won all year. The Jets trailed 21-7 at halftime and stalled at the Miami 1-yard line in the fourth quarter. Coach Aaron Glenn's clock management drew heavy criticism after he burned all three timeouts before the break.

stories.text: Breece Hall is close but still sidelined
stories.summary: Hall has missed nearly a month with a quadriceps injury suffered Sept. 27 against Detroit. He returned to limited practice last week, but Braelon Allen again led the backfield against Miami. The Raiders game on Sunday is his next target.

stories.text: Rookie Omar Cooper Jr. posts back-to-back 100-yard games
stories.summary: Cooper caught five passes for 115 yards and a touchdown against Miami. He is the first Jets rookie with consecutive 100-yard games since Al Toon in 1985. His 5.06 yards per route run leads all receivers with at least 10 catches.

stories.text: 304: rushing yards the Jets allowed in two games
stories.summary: The run defense has given up 304 yards over the last two games. Miami averaged 5.1 yards per carry and held the ball for nearly 35 minutes. The Jets' next opponents will take note.

stories.text: Jets host Raiders Sunday at 1 p.m. ET on Fox
stories.summary: New York hosts Las Vegas at MetLife Stadium on Sunday, Nov. 1, at 1:00 p.m. ET on Fox. The Jets are 2-5 and have lost two straight. Watch whether Hall returns and whether the run defense improves.

teams.name: Baltimore Ravens
teams.headline: Ravens fall apart after halftime at home

stories.text: Ravens blow halftime lead, lose 35-13 to Bengals
stories.summary: Baltimore led at the break, then Cincinnati scored touchdowns on its first five second-half possessions and won the half 35-0. The Ravens went 0-for-3 in the red zone and missed 11 tackles, eight of them after halftime. They have lost two straight and sit last in the AFC North.

stories.text: Lamar Jackson's ankle decides the Buffalo trip
stories.summary: Jackson has missed three straight games with a high ankle sprain, and Tyler Huntley has started all three. Coach Jesse Minter sounded cautiously optimistic Monday and said the team will know more Wednesday. Baltimore has averaged 29 points a game with Jackson and 17.7 with Huntley.

stories.text: Zay Flowers gets 137 yards in a losing effort
stories.summary: Flowers caught eight passes for 137 yards and a touchdown, and 120 of those yards came before halftime. Huntley threw for 298 yards in the game, but a second-half fumble and interception ended the Ravens' chances. Flowers was the one bright spot on an offense that stalled after the break.

stories.text: 35-0: Bengals' second half buries Baltimore
stories.summary: Cincinnati scored on its first five trips after halftime. Baltimore has now given up double-digit leads in back-to-back weeks, and three of its four losses came after it led by double digits. The defense ranks third in EPA per play in the first quarter and 32nd in the fourth.

stories.text: Ravens visit Bills Sunday at 1 p.m. ET on CBS
stories.summary: Baltimore travels to Buffalo for a Week 8 game that could hinge on Jackson's Wednesday practice report. The Ravens need to fix their second-half fades and their red zone trouble fast. Sunday kickoff is 1 p.m. ET on CBS.

teams.name: Cincinnati Bengals
teams.headline: Bengals erase 13-0 hole and rout Baltimore

stories.text: Bengals score 35 unanswered, beat Ravens 35-13
stories.summary: Cincinnati trailed 13-0 at halftime in Baltimore and then scored on every second-half possession it needed. The win is the Bengals' first in the AFC North this season and lifts them to 4-2. The defense racked up four sacks and shut out the Ravens after the break.

stories.text: Erick All hurt his knee, Kyle Dugger is out
stories.summary: Tight end Erick All left the Ravens game with a knee injury, and coach Zac Taylor said more information could come within a day. All has had that knee operated on several times and missed all of 2025. Safety Kyle Dugger hurt his quad and will definitely miss the Titans game.

stories.text: Joe Burrow throws four TDs in a dominant half
stories.summary: Burrow finished 22 of 30 for 292 yards and four touchdowns, all four in the second half. In that half he went 16 of 18 for 249 yards. He now has 15 touchdown passes this season.

stories.text: 4 for 4: Rehkow's punts all land inside the 20
stories.summary: Punter Ryan Rehkow put all four of his punts inside the Ravens' 20 and covered 184 yards doing it. That field position helped Cincinnati's defense pin Baltimore all afternoon. The Bengals also had four sacks, including two from Boye Mafe.

stories.text: Titans visit Cincinnati Sunday at 1 p.m. ET on CBS
stories.summary: Tennessee comes to Paycor Stadium for Week 8 after a 27-24 loss to Cleveland. Kickoff is noon Central, which is 1 p.m. ET, on CBS. Watch how the Bengals' tight end room holds up with All's knee in question.

teams.name: Cleveland Browns
teams.headline: Szmyt kick keeps Browns rolling in Nashville

stories.text: Browns beat Titans 27-24 on last-second field goal
stories.summary: Deshaun Watson hit Harold Fannin Jr. for a 36-yard gain to set up Andre Szmyt's game-winning kick. Cleveland has now won two straight and sits at 5-2. Every Browns win this season has come by four points or less.

stories.text: Grant Delpit gets hit in the head a week after concussion
stories.summary: Safety Grant Delpit left the field with trainers after a hit from a teammate, then returned in the fourth quarter without entering concussion protocol. He had just cleared protocol from a concussion suffered October 18. Defensive tackle Mike Hall Jr. missed a third straight game with an ankle injury.

stories.text: Deshaun Watson delivers again in the fourth quarter
stories.summary: Watson threw for 308 yards and ran for a score as Cleveland came back from a 14-0 deficit. He has led a fourth-quarter or game-winning drive in every Browns victory this season. The Browns will lean on that again in Pittsburgh.

stories.text: 183: Browns' rushing yards fuel a 491-yard day
stories.summary: Cleveland gained 491 total yards and 26 first downs in Nashville, 183 of them on the ground. Watson went 25 of 36 for 308 yards, and rookie KC Concepcion caught eight passes for 129 yards. The Titans' own recap blamed their pass rush for giving Watson too much time.

stories.text: Browns at Steelers, first place on the line Sunday
stories.summary: Cleveland visits Pittsburgh on Sunday, November 1 at 1 p.m. ET on CBS, with both teams at 5-2 and tied atop the AFC North. The Browns already beat the Steelers 27-24 earlier this season. Watch Delpit's availability and whether Cleveland's close-game luck holds.

teams.name: Pittsburgh Steelers
teams.headline: Steelers win in Paris, now eye first place

stories.text: Steelers beat Saints 16-10 in first NFL game in France
stories.summary: Pittsburgh won its third straight at the Stade de France in front of 78,488 fans. Chris Boswell kicked three field goals, and Aaron Rodgers went 19 of 30 for 212 yards and a touchdown. A Tyler Shough interception ended a New Orleans drive to open the second half.

stories.text: T.J. Watt returns after knee bang, Joseph-Day to IR
stories.summary: Watt banged knees with a teammate in Paris, came back and finished with a sack. Running back Rico Dowdle played through a questionable knee, while defensive lineman Sebastian Joseph-Day went on injured reserve with a triceps injury. Safety DeShon Elliott made his season debut after coming off IR.

stories.text: Jaylen Warren runs for 101 yards in Paris
stories.summary: Warren opened with a 29-yard run and finished with 101 rushing yards on 18 carries plus 36 receiving. He has four games with 125 or more scrimmage yards this season, tied for the most in the NFL. He is now the lead back.

stories.text: 10 of 16: Steelers stay on the field on third down
stories.summary: Pittsburgh converted 10 of 16 third downs against New Orleans, many on runs in third-and-short.

stories.text: Browns visit Acrisure Stadium Sunday at 1 p.m. ET on CBS
stories.summary: Both teams are 5-2 and tied for first in the AFC North. Pittsburgh lost 27-24 to Cleveland earlier this season, and the offensive line will need to protect Rodgers better this time. The Steelers have a bye in Week 9.

teams.name: Houston Texans
teams.headline: Texans fall in OT, now rest on a bye

stories.text: Texans drop overtime game to Giants, fall to 2-5
stories.summary: Houston lost 27-21 in overtime to the New York Giants on Sunday, its fifth defeat of the season. Devin Singletary scored the winning touchdown in the extra period. The offense lacked creativity and the defense missed tackles, and the Texans now get a bye to sort it out.

stories.text: Marks leaves with leg injury, returns; Montgomery out
stories.summary: Running back Woody Marks left the game in the third quarter with an apparent leg injury and came back. The Texans had only two active backs because David Montgomery was ruled out with a groin injury before the game. Tank Dell played after a knee layoff of more than 670 days, and the bye gives the team time to heal.

stories.text: To'oTo'o posts 10 tackles in second game back
stories.summary: Linebacker Henry To'oTo'o had 10 tackles, two for loss, a quarterback hit and half a sack against the Giants. It was his second game back from a shoulder injury that cost him four weeks. His tackle total ranked second on the team.

stories.text: 0: Sacks for Will Anderson Jr. in his last two games
stories.summary: Anderson had seven sacks through the first five games. He went without one against the Giants for the second straight week. Houston's pass rush needs him back on track as Malik Nabers piled up a fourth straight 100-yard game against the secondary.

stories.text: Texans on bye in Week 8, then visit the Chargers
stories.summary: Houston is off this week. The next game is at the Los Angeles Chargers on Sunday, November 8 at 4:05 PM ET on CBS. Watch how Marks and Montgomery split carries once both are healthy.

teams.name: Indianapolis Colts
teams.headline: Colts offense stalls in third straight loss

stories.text: Colts lose third straight, 16-10 at Minnesota
stories.summary: Indianapolis fell to 2-5 with a 16-10 loss to the unbeaten Vikings. Will Reichard's 52-yard field goal gave Minnesota a six-point lead late, and Harrison Smith intercepted Daniel Jones on the final Colts possession. Kicker Spencer Shrader missed two kicks, ending a 22-game streak of made field goals.

stories.text: Pierce unavailable; Gardner week-to-week with calf strain
stories.summary: Wide receiver Alec Pierce did not play against the Vikings, and the receiver room felt it. Cornerback Sauce Gardner is week-to-week with a mild calf strain. Linebackers CJ Allen and Bryce Boettcher were inactive with injuries.

stories.text: Jonathan Taylor runs for 95 yards, one 38-yard score
stories.summary: Taylor carried for 95 yards at 5.3 per carry, and 38 of those came on a touchdown run. Without that run he had 57 yards on 17 attempts. He remains the one dependable piece of an offense that managed 3.7 yards per play.

stories.text: 68.9%: Minnesota's blitz rate, the league's highest
stories.summary: Daniel Jones went 11 of 18 for 101 yards and an interception against the Vikings' blitz, a 53.2 passer rating. Among 33 qualifying quarterbacks, he ranks last in sacks taken against the blitz this season.

stories.text: Colts visit first-place Jaguars on Sunday at 1 PM ET
stories.summary: Indianapolis plays at Jacksonville on November 1 at 1:00 PM ET on CBS. The Jaguars have won 11 straight home games against the Colts. Watch whether the offensive line can handle pressure and whether Gardner returns.

teams.name: Jacksonville Jaguars
teams.headline: Jaguars stay in first place during their bye

stories.text: Jaguars win the bye as AFC South rivals all lose
stories.summary: Jacksonville did not play in Week 7 and still gained ground, because Indianapolis, Houston and Tennessee all lost. At 4-2, the Jaguars lead the division by 2.5 games over the Colts and Texans. They return to action at home against the Colts this Sunday.

stories.text: LT Anton Harrison out for the season with torn ACL
stories.summary: Harrison tore the ACL in his right knee and is on injured reserve. He had started 53 games since Jacksonville drafted him 27th overall in 2023. Walker Little, a backup with 40 career starts, is expected to take over at left tackle.

stories.text: Trevor Lawrence has 14 touchdown passes, four picks
stories.summary: Lawrence threw for 306 yards and four touchdowns in London without taking a sack. He carries 14 touchdown passes against four interceptions into the Colts game. Indianapolis ranks last in the league in EPA per rush allowed, which should help the whole offense.

stories.text: 30th: Jaguars' rank in passing yards allowed per game
stories.summary: Jacksonville gives up 273.8 passing yards a game, 30th in the league. Over the last three weeks that number is about 320. The slot has been the problem area, so Keenan Allen and Josh Downs are the Colts targets to watch.

stories.text: Jaguars host Colts Sunday at 1 PM ET on CBS
stories.summary: Jacksonville hosts Indianapolis on November 1 at 1:00 PM ET on CBS at EverBank Stadium. The Jaguars have won 11 straight home games in this series. Cornerback Montaric Brown and safety Antonio Johnson have uncertain status.

teams.name: Tennessee Titans
teams.headline: Titans lose on a last-second field goal

stories.text: Titans blow 14-0 lead, lose 27-24 to Browns
stories.summary: Cleveland's Andre Szmyt kicked a 32-yard field goal as time expired after Cam Ward had tied the game with an 11-play, 63-yard drive. Tennessee fell to 1-6. The Titans failed to score from the Cleveland 1 in the first half, a swing that cost them the game.

stories.text: Spears inactive with knee injury; Townsend hurt
stories.summary: Running back Tyjae Spears was inactive against Cleveland with a knee injury. Punter and holder Tommy Townsend was hurt late in the second quarter but came back to hold for kicks in the fourth quarter. Their status for Cincinnati will come out in this week's practice reports.

stories.text: Tony Pollard runs for 129 yards and three scores
stories.summary: Pollard carried 25 times for 129 yards, 5.2 per carry, and three touchdowns, plus three catches for 26 yards. He had averaged 4.0 yards per carry with one rushing score entering the game. He took 25 of the 28 carries by Titans backs.

stories.text: 2 of 7: Cam Ward's completions on deep throws
stories.summary: ESPN charted Ward at 2 of 7 on deep passes for 44 yards. He finished 20 of 31 for 181 yards, 5.8 per attempt, with an interception. Both deep completions came on the tying drive, to Elic Ayomanor and Carnell Tate.

stories.text: Titans visit Bengals on November 1 at 1 PM ET
stories.summary: Tennessee plays at Cincinnati on Sunday, November 1 at 1:00 PM ET on CBS. The Titans have not won back-to-back games since November 2022. Watch whether Pollard keeps getting the workload with Spears hurt.

teams.name: Denver Broncos
teams.headline: Broncos win three straight, Chiefs up next

stories.text: Broncos beat Cardinals 30-16 for a third straight win
stories.summary: Denver scored in all four quarters for the first time this season and moved to 5-2. Bo Nix bounced back from a rough outing against Seattle, and the offense hit three plays of 40 yards or more. The Chiefs come to town Sunday.

stories.text: Allen and Waddle hurt late in Arizona
stories.summary: Defensive lineman Zach Allen left the game with a hamstring injury and wide receiver Jaylen Waddle left with a chest injury, both in the fourth quarter. Neither returned, and their status for the Chiefs game is unclear. Watch Wednesday's practice report for the first official word.

stories.text: Bo Nix breaks loose for a 62-yard touchdown run
stories.summary: Nix ran for a 62-yard score in Arizona, a play that helped Denver put up its best rushing day in a year. RJ Harvey added a 52-yard screen catch and Marvin Mims Jr. had a 47-yard catch and run. The offense finally stretched the field.

stories.text: 159: rushing yards, Denver's most since last season
stories.summary: The Broncos ran for 159 yards against Arizona, their best total since a win over Dallas last year. Their previous high this season was 106, against the Chargers. Jonah Coleman returned from an ankle injury and gained 54 yards on nine carries.

stories.text: Chiefs visit Denver Sunday at 4:25 p.m. ET on CBS
stories.summary: Denver hosts Kansas City in Week 8 with the AFC West lead in play. The Chiefs arrive off a 20-3 loss in Seattle. The Broncos must clean up 11 penalties from Sunday and learn how healthy Allen and Waddle are.

teams.name: Kansas City Chiefs
teams.headline: Chiefs lose 20-3 in Seattle, first loss of year

stories.text: Seahawks hand Chiefs their first loss, 20-3
stories.summary: Kansas City managed 213 yards and one Harrison Butker field goal on Sunday night in Seattle. Patrick Mahomes threw for 165 yards with an interception and a fumble, and Butker missed two more kicks. Andy Reid said he took full responsibility.

stories.text: Bolton has neck spasms, Moore nears return
stories.summary: Andy Reid said linebacker Nick Bolton had neck spasms but expects him to be fine. Tackle Jaylon Moore, who missed Seattle in the concussion protocol, could clear it this week. Receiver Rashee Rice, out with a hamstring injury, may return to practice in some form next Wednesday.

stories.text: Travis Kelce passes Harrison and Carter on the catch list
stories.summary: Kelce caught four passes against Seattle and reached 1,104 career receptions. That moved him past Marvin Harrison and Cris Carter into fifth in NFL history. It was a small bright spot on a night the offense never found rhythm.

stories.text: 36: rushing yards for Kenneth Walker III against his old team
stories.summary: Walker came in averaging a league-best 133 yards per game and managed 36 on 14 carries in his return to Seattle. The Seahawks have not allowed a 100-yard rusher in 36 games, the longest active streak in the league. Kansas City ran for just 50 yards as a team.

stories.text: Chiefs at Broncos Sunday, 4:25 p.m. ET on CBS
stories.summary: Kansas City heads to Denver for a divisional game off its first loss. The offense needs to protect Mahomes with tackle Josh Simmons on injured reserve and Moore's status in question. Simmons cannot return before Week 11.

teams.name: Las Vegas Raiders
teams.headline: Raiders stay with Cousins after fourth straight loss

stories.text: Kubiak sticks with Cousins over Mendoza
stories.summary: After a 35-21 loss to the Rams, coach Klint Kubiak said the team would look at everything, then committed to Kirk Cousins on Monday. Las Vegas started 3-0 and has lost four in a row. Rookie Fernando Mendoza, the first overall pick, remains the backup.

stories.text: Washington questionable, Bowers back at full practice
stories.summary: Before the Rams game, Brock Bowers (hamstring, calf) went from limited Wednesday to full participation Thursday and Friday. Running back Mike Washington was questionable with a foot and back issue. Tight end Carter Runyon and receiver Dont'e Thornton Jr. were ruled out. This is the latest official report available.

stories.text: Tre Tucker leads Las Vegas with 103 yards and a score
stories.summary: Tucker caught five passes for 103 yards and a touchdown against the Rams. Ashton Jeanty ran for only 15 yards on eight carries but led the team with eight catches for 61 yards and a score. Brock Bowers added six catches for 73 yards.

stories.text: 1 of 5: Raiders' red zone conversions against the Rams
stories.summary: Las Vegas scored on one of five trips inside the 20 and went 3 of 14 on third down, according to Kubiak's comments. Kirk Cousins threw for 295 yards and two touchdowns but the drives stalled near the goal line. Kubiak called the red zone the main problem.

stories.text: Raiders visit the Jets Sunday at 1 p.m. ET on Fox
stories.summary: Las Vegas looks to end a four-game skid on the road against New York. The defense has given up more than 30 points four games running. The offense needs to turn Cousins' league-leading 16 touchdown passes into points near the goal line.

teams.name: Los Angeles Chargers
teams.headline: Winless Chargers use bye to weigh every option

stories.text: Harbaugh says 0-6 Chargers are considering everything
stories.summary: Jim Harbaugh said the winless record rules nothing out as the team uses its bye to re-evaluate. He said the staff may simplify the playbook and pointed to the defense as a strength. The Chargers face the Rams on Nov. 1 coming off a 22-6 loss to Kansas City.

stories.text: Alt and Awosika practice during bye, Slater out until Week 10
stories.summary: Right tackle Joe Alt (neck) and guard Kayode Awosika (fibula) were practicing on Oct. 21 and were preparing to return. Left tackle Rashawn Slater, recovering from a high ankle sprain, is not eligible to play until Week 10 at Baltimore. Center Tyler Biadasz is out for the season with a torn ACL.

stories.text: Rookie Akheem Mesidor gives the defense a lift
stories.summary: Mesidor, the No. 22 overall pick, has 2.5 sacks and a forced fumble through six games. Safety Genesis Smith, another rookie, is tied for the team lead with two interceptions. Five rookies have played in every game.

stories.text: 8: Justin Herbert's interceptions, most in the NFL
stories.summary: Herbert has completed 59.4 percent of his passes with five touchdowns and 10 turnovers. He has also been sacked 21 times, second most in the league. Harbaugh said Herbert has played with desperation at times.

stories.text: Chargers meet the Rams Sunday, 4:05 p.m. ET on Fox
stories.summary: Los Angeles returns from the bye against Matthew Stafford and the Rams at SoFi Stadium. Watch the offensive line, where rookies have started at four spots, and whether Mike McDaniel's offense changes after the bye. The Texans follow on Nov. 8.

teams.name: Dallas Cowboys
teams.headline: Cowboys run past Eagles, win 38-21

stories.text: Cowboys run past Eagles on Monday night
stories.summary: Dallas beat Philadelphia 38-21 at Lincoln Financial Field and moved to 3-4. The Cowboys scored on seven of nine drives, committed no turnovers and finished with 416 total yards. The win snapped a 1-7-1 run in their last nine primetime games.

stories.text: Overshown returns from hamstring, picks off McKee
stories.summary: Linebacker DeMarvion Overshown made his first appearance after a hamstring injury and made it count. He finished with six tackles, a tackle for loss, a pass deflection and the fourth-quarter interception that ended Philadelphia's comeback bid. No new Cowboys injuries surfaced in the postgame coverage.

stories.text: Javonte Williams hits 155 yards, a career high
stories.summary: Williams carried 25 times for 155 yards and a touchdown, a career best. He is Dallas's first 150-yard rusher since Ezekiel Elliott in 2018. The Cowboys ran 38 times for 204 yards after taking criticism for their play calling a week earlier.

stories.text: 204: Cowboys rushing yards against Philadelphia
stories.summary: Dallas ran for 204 yards and converted 8 of 13 third downs. Dak Prescott needed only 15 completions for 212 yards and three touchdowns, two of them to CeeDee Lamb.

stories.text: Cardinals visit Dallas Sunday at 1 p.m. ET on Fox
stories.summary: The Cowboys host Arizona in Week 8 and sit behind the 4-2-1 Giants in the NFC East. Watch whether the ground game that carried Monday night repeats at home. Dallas then travels to Indianapolis in Week 9.

teams.name: New York Giants
teams.headline: Giants take NFC East lead into bye

stories.text: Giants beat Texans in OT, own NFC East lead
stories.summary: Devin Singletary broke a 30-yard touchdown run in overtime to give New York a 27-21 win at Houston. The Giants improved to 4-2-1 and head into their Week 8 bye atop the division. It was J.J. McCarthy's first win as a Giants starter.

stories.text: Tracy and Skattebo hurt hamstrings before the bye
stories.summary: Running back Tyrone Tracy Jr. left in the second quarter with a hamstring injury, and Cam Skattebo reportedly strained a hamstring late. No official designations or timelines are out yet, per Athlon. Linebacker Tremaine Edmunds (shoulder) went on injured reserve, and Jevon Holland and Greg Newsome II sat out with concussions.

stories.text: Skattebo runs for a career-high 124 yards
stories.summary: Skattebo carried 17 times for a career-high 124 yards and a 16-yard touchdown. His 42-yard run set up Singletary's overtime score. Malik Nabers added 7 catches for 111 yards, his fourth straight 100-yard game.

stories.text: 188: Giants rushing yards, four rushing scores
stories.summary: New York ran for 188 yards, a season high, and scored four rushing touchdowns with four different players. The Giants had not done that since 1950. The ground game gave McCarthy easy throws in his first start.

stories.text: Bye in Week 8, then at Eagles Nov. 8, 1 p.m. ET on Fox
stories.summary: The Giants rest this week and use it to heal the backfield. They travel to Philadelphia in Week 9, then host Washington on Thursday night in Week 10. Check the running back reports when practice resumes.

teams.name: Philadelphia Eagles
teams.headline: Eagles lose fifth straight to Cowboys

stories.text: Eagles drop fifth straight, longest skid since 2016
stories.summary: Dallas beat Philadelphia 38-21 and the Eagles fell to 2-5, third in the NFC East. The defense had no sacks, takeaways, tackles for loss or quarterback hits. Philadelphia has allowed at least 375 yards in every game of the streak.

stories.text: Barkley back, Pierce hurt; Hurts out with blood clots
stories.summary: Saquon Barkley returned from a hamstring absence, then left with a back injury after nine snaps. Dameon Pierce and defensive tackle Moro Ojomo got hurt late, and the team had given no updates Tuesday morning. Quarterback Jalen Hurts is on injured reserve with blood clots in his lungs and is expected to miss the season.

stories.text: Rookie Makai Lemon scores first NFL touchdown
stories.summary: Lemon caught seven passes for 67 yards and his first career touchdown. He was the main target for Tanner McKee, who threw for 211 yards with one touchdown and one interception. Lemon worked with DeVonta Smith and Dontayvion Wicks both out.

stories.text: 375: yards allowed in every game of the skid
stories.summary: The Eagles gave up 416 yards and 25 first downs to Dallas. They have allowed at least 375 yards in each of their five straight losses.

stories.text: At Commanders Sunday night, 8:20 p.m. ET on NBC
stories.summary: Philadelphia visits Washington on Nov. 1, then hosts the Giants on Nov. 8 before a bye. Watch the quarterback and running back availability, since Hurts is done and two backs left hurt.

teams.name: Washington Commanders
teams.headline: Commanders off, McLaurin out for season

stories.text: Quinn at a crossroads as Commanders sit on bye
stories.summary: Washington is 1-4-1 after a 23-17 loss at San Francisco and is two games out of first in the NFC East. Dan Quinn has drawn heavy criticism for fourth-down and clock decisions in recent games. The team hired veteran defensive coach Steve Wilks as an adviser this week.

stories.text: McLaurin out for season with torn patellar tendon
stories.summary: Terry McLaurin tore the patellar tendon in his left knee against the 49ers and will have surgery. Quinn said he is done for the year. McLaurin had 15 catches for 230 yards and a touchdown in five games.

stories.text: Jayden Daniels throws for 300 against San Francisco
stories.summary: Daniels completed 29 of 40 passes for 300 yards and two touchdowns with no interceptions against the 49ers. It was his best passer rating of the season at 110.4. He has five touchdowns and no picks this year.

stories.text: 0-3-1: Washington's record in Daniels' starts
stories.summary: The Commanders have not won a game that Daniels started this season. He has played four of six games. The only win came in games he missed.

stories.text: Eagles visit Sunday night, 8:20 p.m. ET on NBC
stories.summary: Washington returns from its bye to host Philadelphia on Nov. 1, then hosts the Rams in Week 9. Both come before the trade deadline. Watch how the offense replaces McLaurin.

teams.name: Chicago Bears
teams.headline: Bears lose Kmet for the season

stories.text: Bears beat Patriots but lose tight end Cole Kmet for the year
stories.summary: Chicago won Thursday night, 30-24, to move to 5-2, but Cole Kmet went down with a right knee injury late in the fourth quarter and is done for the season. Coach Ben Johnson said, "It stinks. I hate it for him." Second-year tight end Colston Loveland and rookie Sam Roush now carry bigger roles.

stories.text: Kmet on IR, rookie Muhammad hurt, three defenders still out
stories.summary: Kmet has been placed on injured reserve with a season-ending knee injury. Rookie Malik Muhammad left the Patriots game with a toe injury. Montez Sweat, Dayo Odeyingbo and T.J. Edwards were already out against New England.

stories.text: Caleb Williams throws for 308 yards without a turnover
stories.summary: Williams completed 22 of 33 passes for 308 yards and two touchdowns with no turnovers, good for a 116.7 rating. Luther Burden III caught four passes for 130 yards and a score, all before halftime. Loveland added seven catches for 69 yards and a touchdown.

stories.text: 58: Cairo Santos wins it from a career-long distance
stories.summary: Santos missed a 53-yard try earlier, then hit a career-long 58-yarder with 1:34 left to beat New England. Chicago ran 66 snaps to the Patriots' 50 and held the ball for 32:24.

stories.text: Bears visit Seahawks on Monday Night Football
stories.summary: Chicago plays at Seattle on Monday, Nov. 2, at 8:15 p.m. ET on ESPN. The Bears will have to find offense without Kmet while the defense stays thin up front.

teams.name: Detroit Lions
teams.headline: Bates kick beats Packers at the gun

stories.text: Lions edge Packers 20-17 on a walk-off field goal
stories.summary: Jake Bates hit a 22-yard field goal as time expired to finish a 10-play, 71-yard drive and beat Green Bay at Ford Field. Detroit improved to 4-2. Brian Branch also intercepted a pass in his first game back from a torn Achilles.

stories.text: St. Brown and Rakestraw hurt ankles, Campbell not worried
stories.summary: Amon-Ra St. Brown tweaked an ankle and Ennis Rakestraw Jr. left the Packers game with an ankle injury. Dan Campbell said the team does not expect a significant absence for either. St. Brown is set for a Wednesday off day and a return to practice Thursday.

stories.text: Jameson Williams scores twice against Green Bay
stories.summary: Williams caught five passes for 91 yards and touchdowns of 16 and 10 yards. Amon-Ra St. Brown had nine catches for 153 yards, and Jahmyr Gibbs ran 29 times for 116 yards. Williams gave Jared Goff two scoring targets on a day Detroit needed them.

stories.text: 29: Goff extends his touchdown pass streak
stories.summary: Jared Goff threw two touchdown passes to stretch his streak of games with a scoring throw to 29. He went 22 of 32 for 303 yards and has not thrown an interception in six games this season.

stories.text: Unbeaten Vikings visit Ford Field
stories.summary: Detroit hosts 6-0 Minnesota on Sunday, Nov. 1, at 1 p.m. ET on Fox. The Lions' healthy ankles and a defense that has to slow a team that blitzes constantly are the things to watch.

teams.name: Green Bay Packers
teams.headline: Packers fall to last place in North

stories.text: Packers waste chances and lose 20-17 in Detroit
stories.summary: Green Bay dropped to 4-3 and sits last in a division where all four teams are above .500. Rookie kicker Trey Smack missed two short field goals, and the Packers got no points after stopping Detroit on fourth-and-1 at the Lions' 22. Matt LaFleur also regretted going for it on fourth down instead of tying the game with a field goal.

stories.text: Center spot is thin as eight Packers show on injury report
stories.summary: Starting center Sean Rhyan (ankle) did not participate in Monday's estimated report, and backup Jacob Monk (quad) also left the Lions game early. Devonte Wyatt, Zaire Franklin, Travis Glover and Matthew Golden were also listed as non-participants. The Packers did not practice Monday, so the designations are estimates.

stories.text: John Williams steps in at center for his NFL debut
stories.summary: With Rhyan and Monk both hurt, John Williams, a second-year seventh-round pick, played center in his first NFL game and drew praise. Green Bay ran for just 60 yards in the loss. Jordan Love threw for 274 yards and two touchdowns with one interception.

stories.text: 8: roughing the passer flags against Green Bay this year
stories.summary: Two more roughing the passer penalties hit the Packers in Detroit, including one on Karl Brooks during the winning drive. That makes eight on the season against Green Bay, and opponents have none. LaFleur declined to say much about the officiating.

stories.text: Panthers come to Lambeau on a short week
stories.summary: Green Bay hosts Carolina on Thursday, Oct. 29, at 8:15 p.m. ET on Prime Video. The Packers must fix their kicking and line depth in three days.

teams.name: Minnesota Vikings
teams.headline: Last unbeaten team in the NFL

stories.text: Vikings beat Colts 16-10 and stand alone at 6-0
stories.summary: Minnesota is the league's only unbeaten team after the 49ers and Chiefs lost in Week 7. Harrison Smith's interception of Daniel Jones sealed the win. The offense remains the question, with Kevin O'Connell saying the group is "catching our stride."

stories.text: Left guard Donovan Jackson is out for the regular season
stories.summary: Jackson, a second-year first-round pick, tore his meniscus in the win over Miami and needs surgery. Joe Huber, an undrafted second-year lineman from Wisconsin, took over at left guard. He has been out since the Oct. 5 announcement.

stories.text: Kyler Murray manages the game with 150 passing yards
stories.summary: Murray threw for 150 yards as Minnesota gained 275 total yards and held Indianapolis to 218. O'Connell has asked for steady growth from the offense, and the Vikings have scored 125 points through six games. Murray makes plays but has not found consistency yet.

stories.text: 85.2%: Flores blitzes Daniel Jones on nearly every snap
stories.summary: Brian Flores sent extra rushers on 85.2% of Jones' dropbacks, the highest blitz rate by any defense since Next Gen Stats began tracking in 2016. Minnesota pressured Jones on 60.9% of those blitzes, and all four sacks came on blitzes.

stories.text: Vikings put the perfect record on the line in Detroit
stories.summary: Minnesota plays at 4-2 Detroit on Sunday, Nov. 1, at 1 p.m. ET on Fox. After that come the Bills, the Packers and the 49ers, so the next four weeks decide how real this start is.

teams.name: Atlanta Falcons
teams.headline: Falcons upset unbeaten 49ers 29-20

stories.text: Falcons knock off unbeaten 49ers 29-20
stories.summary: Atlanta snapped a two-game losing streak and handed San Francisco its first loss. The Falcons trailed 14-3, then took control with Kyle Pitts' 5-yard touchdown to start the second half. Rookie linebacker Kendal Daniels sealed it with an interception and a fumble recovery, a week after a scary neck injury.

stories.text: Brian Robinson out; secondary gets bodies back
stories.summary: Running back Brian Robinson Jr. missed the 49ers game with a hamstring injury, and Khalil Herbert filled in from the practice squad. Linebacker Divine Deablo, safety Billy Bowman Jr. and rookie corner Avieon Terrell also sat out. A.J. Terrell and C.J. Henderson returned, and Drake London came back after a concussion check in the third quarter.

stories.text: Penix throws 3 TDs without a sack
stories.summary: Michael Penix Jr. completed 25 of 34 passes for 213 yards and three touchdowns with no interceptions. The line allowed no sacks and no hurries, a big change from the five sacks he took against Chicago a week earlier. He has completed at least 72 percent of his passes in each of Atlanta's three wins.

stories.text: 23: unanswered points Atlanta scored on SF
stories.summary: The Falcons trailed 14-3 before outscoring San Francisco 23-0 to lead 26-14. They also won the turnover battle 4-0, even though the 49ers outgained them 400-295. Atlanta's offense moved the ball with short, accurate throws and gave up nothing in protection.

stories.text: At Tampa Bay Sunday, 1 p.m. ET on Fox
stories.summary: Atlanta visits Raymond James Stadium on Nov. 1 for its first meeting with Tampa Bay this season. The Falcons lead the all-time series 33-32, and the last six meetings were each decided by six points or fewer. Watch whether Atlanta's patched-up backfield holds up against a Bucs run game that just piled up 258 yards.

teams.name: Carolina Panthers
teams.headline: Panthers routed 43-13 by Tampa Bay

stories.text: Bucs run all over Panthers in 43-13 loss
stories.summary: Tampa Bay rushed 49 times for 258 yards and three touchdowns as Carolina lost its second game in three weeks. Coach Dave Canales said he liked the calls on defense but not the execution. Carolina entered the week last in the NFL in run defense at 153.2 yards allowed per game.

source.name: Associated Press via Bozeman Daily Chronicle

stories.text: Right tackle Taylor Moton breaks fibula
stories.summary: Moton hurt his ankle and fibula against Tampa Bay, just two games after returning from blood clots in his lungs. Canales said he will miss quite a bit of time. First-round rookie Monroe Freeling moves into the starting right tackle spot.

source.name: Associated Press via Bozeman Daily Chronicle

stories.text: Bryce Young has his worst day of the year
stories.summary: Young was 14 of 27 for 163 yards with one touchdown and two interceptions, and Tampa Bay sacked him five times. He also lost a fumble that Calijah Kancey returned for a touchdown. Young entered the game leading the NFL at 305.8 passing yards per game.

stories.text: 153.2: rushing yards Carolina allows per game
stories.summary: That figure is the most in the NFL and came before Tampa Bay ran for 258 more. The Panthers gave up 291 rushing yards and six rushing touchdowns in Week 1 against Chicago. They held opponents to 92.5 yards per game over the next four weeks, so Sunday looked like a step back.

source.name: Associated Press via Bozeman Daily Chronicle

stories.text: At Green Bay Thursday, 8:15 p.m. ET on Prime Video
stories.summary: Carolina plays on a short week at Lambeau Field on Thursday, Oct. 29. The Panthers are 5-10 in Thursday night games since 1995. Green Bay averages the fewest rushing yards in the league at 59.9 per game, so the Carolina run defense gets a chance to bounce back.

source.name: Associated Press via Bozeman Daily Chronicle

teams.name: New Orleans Saints
teams.headline: Saints fall in Paris, head to bye at 2-5

stories.text: Steelers beat Saints 16-10 in first NFL game in France
stories.summary: New Orleans dropped to 2-5 at Stade de France and now takes its bye week. The Saints trailed 13-10 at halftime and never found a way to take the lead. Coach Kellen Moore said a team that runs 17 times for 18 yards will struggle to win.

stories.text: Donaldson and Reid hurt in Paris
stories.summary: Running back CJ Donaldson left in the first half with a shoulder injury. Safety Justin Reid was ruled out with a concussion just before halftime. Offensive lineman Cesar Ruiz and defensive lineman Nathan Shepherd were inactive, and the bye week gives all of them time to heal.

stories.text: Tyler Shough throws for 278 yards in the loss
stories.summary: Shough completed 30 of 38 passes for 278 yards and a 1-yard touchdown to Devaughn Vele. His one interception came on the first drive of the second half, with the Saints down 13-10. Alvin Kamara caught seven passes for 57 yards, and rookie Barion Brown had a 49-yard catch.

stories.text: 18: rushing yards on 17 carries for New Orleans
stories.summary: The Saints could not run the ball against Pittsburgh, and Shough's three carries produced 7 of those yards. Pittsburgh ran for 148 on the other side, led by Jaylen Warren's 101 yards. Pittsburgh converted 10 of 16 third downs.

stories.text: On bye, then Browns on Nov. 8 at 1 p.m. ET on CBS
stories.summary: New Orleans is off in Week 8 and returns home to face Cleveland at Caesars Superdome. Moore said the staff will evaluate what is not working and take the emotion out of it. The run game is the first thing to fix.

teams.name: Tampa Bay Buccaneers
teams.headline: Bucs blow out Panthers 43-13 on the ground

stories.text: Bucs crush Panthers 43-13 to break out of skid
stories.summary: Tampa Bay scored on offense, defense and special teams and won by 30 after a 1-5 start. Baker Mayfield said the win was a statement to themselves, not to the rest of the NFC South. The Bucs held the ball for nearly 36 minutes.

stories.text: Mayfield back; Egbuka, Goedeke, Winfield out
stories.summary: Mayfield returned from a dislocated right thumb that cost him three games and said he felt no worse after the game. Wide receiver Emeka Egbuka (concussion and foot), tackle Luke Goedeke (calf) and safety Antoine Winfield Jr. (rib) were ruled out on Friday's report. Their status for Atlanta is the next thing to watch.

stories.text: Yaya Diaby records three sacks
stories.summary: Diaby had three of Tampa Bay's five sacks, his first career three-sack game. It was the first for a Bucs player since Devin White in December 2020. Bucky Irving added 106 yards and two rushing touchdowns on 24 carries.

stories.text: 11: pass attempts for Mayfield in a 43-13 win
stories.summary: Mayfield threw only 11 passes, the fewest in a Bucs win in 46 years, while the team rushed 49 times for 258 yards. Mayfield went 7 of 11 for 64 yards and a touchdown. The Bucs are now 14-0 when they carry the ball 46 or more times.

stories.text: Falcons visit Sunday, 1 p.m. ET on Fox
stories.summary: Tampa Bay hosts Atlanta at Raymond James Stadium on Nov. 1. The Bucs have recorded five sacks in back-to-back games, and five more would tie the team record for consecutive five-sack games. Atlanta leads the all-time series 33-32.

teams.name: Arizona Cardinals
teams.headline: Cardinals lose 10th straight at home

stories.text: Cardinals fall to Broncos 30-16, 10th straight home loss
stories.summary: Arizona dropped to 2-5 after Denver beat it 30-16 at State Farm Stadium on Sunday. The Cardinals have now lost 10 consecutive home games. The defense has given up 30 or more points in five of its last six games, and Arizona has allowed the most points in the league through seven weeks.

stories.text: Jeremiyah Love set to return to practice Wednesday
stories.summary: Running back Jeremiyah Love sat out the last two games with a left ankle injury. Coach Mike LaFleur said Monday that Love will practice Wednesday, and he has a good chance to play at Dallas on Sunday. If he is cleared, he should take back the lead role in the backfield.

stories.text: Brissett keeps the job after a day under siege
stories.summary: Jacoby Brissett faced pressure on 50.9 percent of his dropbacks against Denver, and Nik Bonitto alone had 13 pressures. Brissett took 2.82 seconds to throw, his slowest time of the season. LaFleur has confirmed Brissett will start at Dallas, though questions about rookie Carson Beck are growing.

stories.text: 42.8%: Arizona's red zone touchdown rate, last in the NFL
stories.summary: The Cardinals went 1 for 5 in the red zone against Denver. They have scored one touchdown in their last 10 red zone trips. LaFleur called the problem shared by coaches and players.

stories.text: Cardinals visit the Cowboys on Sunday at 1 PM ET on Fox
stories.summary: Arizona travels to Dallas for Week 8 on Sunday, Nov. 1, with kickoff at 1:00 PM ET on Fox. Brissett is the starter. Watch whether Love returns and whether the offense can finish drives inside the 20. Arizona then plays at Seattle in Week 9.

teams.name: Los Angeles Rams
teams.headline: Rams run past Raiders to end skid

stories.text: Rams beat Raiders 35-21 to snap a two-game losing streak
stories.summary: Los Angeles led 28-6 at halftime after four straight touchdown drives and cruised to a 35-21 win in Las Vegas. The Rams moved to 3-4. They ran for a season-high yardage total and controlled the game on the ground.

stories.text: Puka Nacua's calf MRI shows nothing significant
stories.summary: Nacua entered Sunday questionable with a calf injury he suffered in Thursday's practice, then played and finished with eight catches for 68 yards and a touchdown. He said an MRI showed nothing significant. Davante Adams is not expected back until around the bye week. Corner Trent McDuffie (groin) and linebacker Nate Landman (concussion) were on the pregame report.

stories.text: Stafford passes his way into the Rams record book
stories.summary: Matthew Stafford threw three touchdown passes in the first half and set the franchise record for passing touchdowns with 155 as a Ram. He also has 282 with Detroit. The record came in a win that snapped a two-game slide.

stories.text: 199: rushing yards for the Rams, a season high
stories.summary: Kyren Williams ran 16 times for 99 yards and a touchdown. Blake Corum added 17 carries for 93 yards and a score. More than half of the Rams' 386 yards came on the ground.

stories.text: Rams host the Chargers Sunday at 4:05 PM ET on Fox
stories.summary: Los Angeles plays at home against the Chargers in Week 8 on Sunday, Nov. 1, at 4:05 PM ET on Fox. Watch whether the run game keeps carrying the offense and how the injury list shakes out. The Rams then travel to Washington in Week 9.

teams.name: San Francisco 49ers
teams.headline: 49ers lose first game, 29-20 at Atlanta

stories.text: 49ers suffer first loss, 29-20 at Atlanta, on four turnovers
stories.summary: San Francisco fell to 6-1 against the Falcons despite outgaining them 400 yards to 295. Brock Purdy threw two interceptions, and the 49ers gave the ball away four times without forcing a turnover. The team now heads into its bye week.

stories.text: McCaffrey has a mild hamstring strain, bye may help others
stories.summary: Kyle Shanahan said Christian McCaffrey has a mild hamstring strain and the team is pretty optimistic about his availability after the bye. Nick Bosa, Mike Evans, Deebo Samuel, Garret Wallow, Luke Gifford and Marques Sigle are among those who could return after the break, though none are guaranteed. Shanahan will check their status early next week.

stories.text: Rookie Kaelon Black scores first NFL touchdown
stories.summary: Black found the end zone for the first time in the NFL against Atlanta, and he saw extra carries once McCaffrey briefly left with a thigh contusion. McCaffrey also scored. With the receiver room thin, the backfield carried more of the load.

stories.text: 4: giveaways, and zero takeaways, sank the 49ers
stories.summary: San Francisco outgained Atlanta 400 to 295 and reached Atlanta territory on all nine drives, but scored only 20 points. Atlanta ran off 23 unanswered points. The 49ers also pressured Atlanta on just 3 of 34 dropbacks.

stories.text: 49ers are on bye in Week 8, then host the Raiders
stories.summary: San Francisco has no game in Week 8. The 49ers return Sunday, Nov. 8, at 4:25 PM ET on Fox against the Raiders at home. Watch the trade market at receiver and defensive line and the health of the injured stars.

teams.name: Seattle Seahawks
teams.headline: Seahawks smother Chiefs 20-3

stories.text: Seahawks stifle the Chiefs 20-3 on Sunday night
stories.summary: Seattle improved to 4-3 and ended a two-game losing streak. The defense held Kansas City to 213 yards and 11 first downs, and the Chiefs never reached the red zone, a first in a Patrick Mahomes start. The offense ran for 153 yards and converted 11 of 16 third downs.

stories.text: Cross and Shaheed monitored; Charbonnet eyes Bears game
stories.summary: Left tackle Charles Cross left the Chiefs game with an ankle injury, and receiver Rashid Shaheed has a knee issue. Both will be monitored through the week. Running back Zach Charbonnet, who is coming back from a knee injury, was held out Sunday and could make his season debut against Chicago.

stories.text: Jaxon Smith-Njigba posts 150 yards, six 100-yard games
stories.summary: Smith-Njigba caught nine passes for 150 yards, including a 28-yard touchdown. It was his sixth 100-yard game of the season. He leads all NFL receivers in catches, receiving yards and receiving touchdowns.

stories.text: 213: yards Seattle allowed to Mahomes and the Chiefs
stories.summary: Kansas City managed 11 first downs and one field goal on eight possessions. The Chiefs did not get inside Seattle's 20. Derick Hall added a sack and a forced fumble, and Ty Okada intercepted Mahomes.

stories.text: Seahawks host the Bears Monday at 8:15 PM ET on ESPN
stories.summary: Seattle plays Chicago at Lumen Field on Monday, Nov. 2, at 8:15 PM ET on ESPN. Watch the Cross and Shaheed updates and whether Charbonnet makes his debut. The Seahawks host Arizona the following week.
